classification.difficultyReason: Complete a supplied two-stage tree without replacement, preserving separate red-sock branches, then count favourable outcomes.

inlines.text: A drawer contains two red socks (R), one blue sock (B) and one yellow sock (Y).
Two socks are selected at random

spec.description: Four first-stage branches and three second-stage branches per first-stage branch. Separate first-stage branches represent the two red socks. All supplied labels and outcomes are retained. Ordinary source response boxes become handwriting-sized dotted blanks.
spec.mathematics: First-stage labels R, R, B, Y; second-stage labels R,B,Y beneath each R, R,R,Y beneath B, and R,R,B beneath Y. Twelve equally likely ordered physical-sock outcomes.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied labels R,R,B; R,B,Y,R; and outcomes RR,RB are visible. All other labels and outcomes are blank.

answer.short: First sock: R, R, B, Y. Second-sock labels and outcomes, from top to bottom: R–RR, B–RB, Y–RY; R–RR, B–RB, Y–RY; R–BR, R–BR, Y–BY; R–YR, R–YR, B–YB.
answer.worked: Each first branch represents one physical sock. After it is selected, three socks remain. The completed tree therefore has $4\times3=12$ equally likely paths. Repeated colour outcomes remain on separate paths because the two red socks are distinct socks.

spec.description: Complete self-contained solution tree, preserving all twelve paths and duplicate colour outcomes.
spec.answerVisibility: All missing first-stage, second-stage and outcome labels are completed.

children.label: i
children.prompt: a red sock and a blue sock

answer.worked:
There are two RB paths and two BR paths.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{red and blue})&=\frac{4}{12}\\&=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: any pair of socks of the same colour

answer.worked:
Only two red socks can form a same-colour pair. There are two RR paths.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{2}{12}\\&=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: iv
children.prompt: any pair of socks of different colour

answer.worked:
Ten of the twelve paths have different colours.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{different colours})&=\frac{10}{12}\\&=\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}$$
